title: Hom-complex composition and its agreement with the derived adjunction
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small in the chosen module universe [def-weil-size-convention], with $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived localization $Q$ with category $D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the Hom complex $\mathcal Hom^\bullet$ [def-pur-hom-complex], total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], K-flat complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex], and $H=R\mathcal Hom$ with its fixed K-injective augmentations $\eta_F:F\to I(F)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Fix the closed symmetric monoidal structure and its canonical K-flat tensor and uncurrying models [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model, lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. Write $\operatorname{tr}$ for its right-tensor adjunction and $\epsilon_{L,M}:H(L,M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}L\to M$ for its counit. Write $O=\mathcal O[0]$ and also $O$ for its derived image. For $K,L,M\in D(\mathcal O)$ define
$$c_{K,L,M}=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\epsilon_{L,M}\circ(1\otimes\epsilon_{K,L})\circ\alpha\bigr):H(L,M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}H(K,L)\to H(K,M),$$
where $\alpha$ rebrackets $(H(L,M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}H(K,L))\otimes^{\mathbf L}K$. This family is natural contravariantly in $K$, covariantly in $M$, and dinatural in $L$: for $u:L\to L'$,
$$c_{K,L',M}\circ(1\otimes H(K,u))=c_{K,L,M}\circ(H(u,M)\otimes1)$$
as maps from $H(L',M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}H(K,L)$ to $H(K,M)$. It agrees with derived Hom-complex composition as follows. For arbitrary complexes $E,J,I$, there is a unique chain map
$$\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal Hom^\bullet(J,I)\otimes\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,J))\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,I)$$
whose local homogeneous formula is $f\otimes g\mapsto f\circ g$, without an extra sign. If $J,I$ are K-injective and $t:T\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,J)$ is a K-flat resolution, the localization of the composite of $1\otimes t$ with this chain map represents $c_{QE,QJ,QI}$ under the canonical tensor and Hom comparisons. No boundedness or perfectness is required.

source.place: Tags 0A91 (lemma-composition), 0A98 (lemma-internal-hom-composition), with section-hom-complexes and lemma-internal-hom; identification with the normalized adjunction and dinaturality.

proof.text: Put $e_{K,L,M}=\epsilon_{L,M}(1\otimes\epsilon_{K,L})\alpha$, so that $c=\operatorname{tr}(e)$. The natural bijection of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] is injective and sends a map $v:X\to H(K,M)$ back to $\epsilon_{K,M}(v\otimes1)$. Consequently equality of maps into $H(K,M)$ can be checked after this operation. For $b:M\to M'$, naturality of the counit in its target gives $b\epsilon_{L,M}=\epsilon_{L,M'}(H(L,b)\otimes1)$, whence $b e_{K,L,M}=e_{K,L,M'}(H(L,b)\otimes1\otimes1)$. Naturality of transposition gives $H(K,b)c_{K,L,M}=c_{K,L,M'}(H(L,b)\otimes1)$. For $a:K'\to K$, the parameter naturality of the same adjunction gives $\epsilon_{K,L}(1\otimes a)=\epsilon_{K',L}(H(a,L)\otimes1)$. Substitute this in $e$ and transpose to obtain $H(a,M)c_{K,L,M}=c_{K',L,M}(1\otimes H(a,L))$. Associators in these equations are the fixed natural associators.

source.place: Tag 0A98 (lemma-internal-hom-composition), omitted functoriality, expanded using the fixed adjunction of Tag 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom).

proof.text: For $u:L\to L'$, uncurry both sides of the asserted dinaturality equation against $K$. Naturality in the target gives $\epsilon_{K,L'}(H(K,u)\otimes1)=u\epsilon_{K,L}$. Parameter naturality gives $\epsilon_{L,M}(H(u,M)\otimes1)=\epsilon_{L',M}(1\otimes u)$. Thus both uncurried maps, from $(H(L',M)\otimes H(K,L))\otimes K$ to $M$, are $\epsilon_{L',M}(1\otimes u)(1\otimes\epsilon_{K,L})\alpha$. Injectivity of the adjunction proves the equation, for arbitrary derived $u$, with no choice of a chain representative.

source.place: Tags 0A98 and 08J9: omitted functoriality, expanded by the two counit naturality identities.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal H(X,Y)=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(X,Y)$. For degrees $p,q,a$, send local homogeneous $f\in\mathcal H(J,I)^p$, $g\in\mathcal H(E,J)^q$ to the family with $a$-component $f^{a+q}\circ g^a:E^a\to I^{a+q+p}$. This is $\mathcal O$-bilinear and commutes with restriction to every slice. The sectionwise tensor universal property and [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] therefore give a morphism on each sheaf tensor summand. Assemble these morphisms using the total direct sum and the target Hom product. An input uses only finitely many total summands; there is no infinite summation over the Hom-product coordinates. The universal properties of sheafification, coproduct and product also prove that this graded map, denoted $m$, is the unique one with the stated local formula.

source.place: Tag 0A91 (lemma-composition): direct construction following More on Algebra Tag 0A8I (lemma-composition); sheafification Tag 03CY.

proof.text:
For homogeneous degrees $|f|=p$, $|g|=q$, expand the two Hom differentials:
$$d(f\circ g)=d_I f g-(-1)^{p+q}f g d_E
=(d_I f-(-1)^p f d_J)g+(-1)^p f(d_Jg-(-1)^q g d_E).$$
The two $f d_Jg$ terms cancel. This is precisely $m(d f\otimes g+(-1)^p f\otimes d g)$, the total-tensor differential. Equality on the sheafification units and every Hom projection proves equality of sheaf morphisms. Hence $m$ is a chain map, with no extra sign. The same construction gives evaluation $\operatorname{ev}_{X,Y}:\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal H(X,Y)\otimes X)\to Y$, $f\otimes x\mapsto f(x)$: the equality $(df)(x)+(-1)^p f(dx)=d_Y(f(x))$ checks its differential. Both constructions commute strictly with precomposition and postcomposition by chain maps, by associativity of their component maps.

source.place: Tags 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), 0A91 (lemma-composition), and More on Algebra 0A8I, displayed differential calculation.

proof.text: Now suppose $J,I$ are K-injective. Put $A=\mathcal H(J,I)$, $B=\mathcal H(E,J)$, $C=\mathcal H(E,I)$, and let $t:T\to B$ be the given K-flat resolution. Choose quasi-isomorphisms $s:P\to E$ and $r:U\to A$ with $P,U$ K-flat by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined], precomposition by $s$ into $J$ or $I$ gives quasi-isomorphisms. The maps $\mathcal H(X,I)\to\mathcal H(X,I(I))$ induced by $\eta_I$, and likewise with $J$, are quasi-isomorphisms because both source and target injective representatives are K-injective. Their localizations give precisely the canonical comparisons to the fixed $H$ of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. In particular $QA,QB,QC$ represent $H(QJ,QI),H(QE,QJ),H(QE,QI)$, and $Qt,Qs,Qr$ are invertible. The canonical comparison $Q\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes T)\cong QA\otimes^{\mathbf L}QT$ is valid although $A$ need not be K-flat: [lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor] requires only one factor to be K-flat.

Form $V=\operatorname{Tot}(T\otimes P)$ and the chain map $h:V\to J$ given by $h(z\otimes x)=t(z)(s(x))$, using the evaluation of step 4. The chain map $T\to\mathcal H(P,I(J))$ obtained from $t$ by precomposition with $s$ and postcomposition with $\eta_J$ has uncurrying $\eta_J h$. Since $T,P$ are K-flat, the normalization of [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model], supplied for the fixed adjunction by [lem-sf-ringed-derived-tensor-hom-adjunction], identifies its derived uncurrying with $Q(\eta_J h)$ followed by $(Q\eta_J)^{-1}$, hence with $Qh$. Under the Hom comparisons of step 5 this says exactly that $Qh$ is $\epsilon_{QE,QJ}(Qt\otimes Qs)$, with the canonical tensor comparison understood. Also $V$ is K-flat, since the fixed model states closure of total tensor under K-flatness.

source.place: Tags 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom), 0A95 and 0A98; the stipulated representative normalization, applied to T and P.

proof.text: Precompose Hom with the chain map $h$ and then with $r$ to obtain $k:U\to\mathcal H(V,I)$, namely $k(u)(z\otimes x)=r(u)(t(z)(s(x)))$. Postcompose with $\eta_I$ when using the fixed replacement. Both $U,V$ are K-flat. The same normalized uncurrying therefore identifies the map represented by $(u\otimes(z\otimes x))\mapsto r(u)(t(z)(s(x)))$ into $I$ with $\epsilon_{QV,QI}((H(Qh,QI)\,Qr)\otimes1)$. Here $Qr$ includes the canonical identification $QA\cong H(QJ,QI)$. Naturality of the counit in its tensor parameter rewrites this as $\epsilon_{QJ,QI}(Qr\otimes Qh)$. By step 6 this is the composite of the two derived evaluations defining $e_{QE,QJ,QI}$, after precomposition by $Qr\otimes Qt\otimes Qs$. Thus the stipulated closed composition has this explicit triple-evaluation transpose.

source.place: Tags 08J9 and 0A98: comparison with double evaluation via parameter naturality and normalized uncurrying on U,V.

proof.text: Let $d=m\circ(1_A\otimes t):\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes T)\to C$ be the chain map in the statement. Put $W=\operatorname{Tot}(U\otimes T)$, which is K-flat by the fixed model. Precompose $d$ with $r\otimes1_T$, then apply $\mathcal H(s,I)$ and $\mathcal H(P,\eta_I)$. This gives a chain map $\phi:W\to\mathcal H(P,I(I))$. Its uncurrying on $((u\otimes z)\otimes x)$ is $\eta_I(r(u)(t(z)(s(x))))$. Normalize now with the K-flat pair $W,P$ and cancel $Q\eta_I$. The transpose of the map induced by $Qd$, after precomposition by $Qr$ and replacement of $QE$ by $QP$, is therefore the same triple evaluation as in step 7. The tensor comparisons preserve the associator by [lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor], so the two bracketings used in steps 7 and 8 give equal maps. Injectivity of the closed adjunction, invertibility of $Qr,Qs,Qt$, and the Hom comparisons of step 5 prove that $Qd$ represents $c_{QE,QJ,QI}$. This proof allowed the given arbitrary K-flat $T$ throughout; it imposed no boundedness, flat-term assumption on $T$, or perfectness.
